analysis: Examined the only supplied change: the test fixture in provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDOwnedEntryRetirementTests.swift (hunks at head lines ~46-66). The SSDEvictableStore conformance now declares retireOwnedEntries(_:unusedSince:), and the private retire helper forwards an optional unusedSince cutoff to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove. This is a test-only signature adaptation that mirrors a production-side API change not included in this batch. No production code, no new attack surface, and no weakened control is visible. Relevant threat is T-041 (SSD prefix-cache at-rest retention, 30-minute sliding TTL, SEC-035). The cutoff lets TTL retirement spare entries that were hit after the cutoff. Without a cutoff, retirement stays unconditional, which is the fail-safe default for the existing callers. A finding is not supportable from test code alone. Unverified contracts, since the production source is outside the supplied evidence, which replays only part of the scope (omitted_units=2, complete=false): (1) SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove(unusedSince:) must not let the cutoff or the in-memory hit extend retention beyond the 30-minute TTL, for example by recording a hit into mtime in a way that postpones expiry indefinitely. (2) Any mtime rewrite that records a hit must keep no-follow and symlink safety, such as setAttributesIfSafe. (3) The epoch-barrier and ownership checks must still run on every retirement path, including a TTL sweep that skips recently hit entries. (4) The SSDEvictableStore callers (SSDBlockStore, SSDDiskBudget, the TTL sweeper) must pass the cutoff only for TTL expiry and never for LRU or budget eviction or for corrupt-file removal. A deeper pass over the production diff is recommended.
